interpretations_recorded_at_freeze2: next-action rows 5-9: a per-height gate that fails only through noise (every failing comparison UNRESOLVED by the power requirement, or G6m's resolution test) is a noise failure and takes row 8 whichever gate it is; rows 6, 7 and 9 need a resolved disagreement (a sign failure counts as resolved). Reason: row 8 names the noise diagnosis, and the power requirement of G8m at s = 0.25 is stricter than G6m's, so the literal gate order would route every noise failure to row 7 (baseline realisation), which an UNRESOLVED comparison cannot show. Recorded before any registered output exists.
the row is the smallest row over the failing per-height gates in scope (all heights for NO_GO, h/c 0.09 for GO_FINE30_ATTACHED)
every per-height gate checks all its listed inputs before computing, so a failed input fails the gate even when another input is lost (registration section 6 input rule)

a MECHANICAL_FAIL among cases that are not gate inputs (shape, linear blend, coa30 sweep) is reported with the next action as mechanical_fail_outside_gate_inputs (section 8: a result, never an amendment) and does not change the row

a case whose checkMesh fails is not solved (status checkMesh_FAILED, MECHANICAL_FAIL either way); a missing base copy is GENERATOR_FAILED and a missing base topology BASE_TOPOLOGY_MISSING (both mechanical)
SHAPE_RESOLVED_CONSISTENT's four conditions are resolution, linearity, med30 vs fine30 agreement and morph vs remesh agreement; the expected sign is reported, not part of the label
G6R and G3bR apply the G6/G3b rules with this registration's sigma_eff, delta and power requirement; G3bR includes the sign at h/c 0.224

the remeshed 0-deg sweep case is the 0-deg point of every remeshed scan; the kernel-M baseline is the 0-deg point of every morphed scan and of the shape scans' med30/fine30 sigma; the kernel-S baselines are the shape scans' 0 mm points

Kaggle-side storage was complete in smoke 2 (the 429 is a download-rate limit). Locally the tar is checked against DONE, extracted with tarfile's 'data' filter and every manifest entry is checked; the evidence holds the extracted files, not the tar.
